title: DeliveryEnvelope
description: The app<->infra delivery seam (RFC-110 / ADR-145). The app (learning-player server) produces envelopes into an outbox; the infra delivery service (issue #1412) drains, renders, and delivers them. Channel-agnostic, idempotent. The payload is fully pre-assembled and EXTRACTIVE (D6: no request-time LLM) and MUST carry the graph (graph_refs), never a flat clip.

id.description: Idempotency key, app-generated. The delivery service MUST dedupe on this.

not_before.description: Do not deliver before this instant (cadence pacing).

expires_at.description: TTL (required) — the delivery service MUST NOT deliver after this instant, so a homelab-down window does not flush stale digests on recovery. The assembler sets it to not_before + one cadence period. Seam v1.1 (2026-08-04).

push_subscription.description: W3C PushSubscription JSON (endpoint + keys). Opaque to the app.

unsubscribe_ref.description: Opaque, rotatable. The delivery service embeds this in the one-click unsubscribe link.

graphRef.description: A canonical KG reference (mirrors the shipped AppEntityRef). This is how a surface 'carries the graph'.

digestItem.description: One resurfaced/highlighted moment. MUST carry graph_refs + a deep_link (moat rule).
digestItem.$comment: additionalProperties:false is load-bearing: it walls off the in-app-only fields the GET /api/app/your-week route adds for card rendering (image_url artwork backdrop, and a backfilled episode_title for topic-centric trending items). Those are route-local enrichments — the assembler MUST NOT write them into the envelope (they would fail validation here), and the delivery worker renders from graph_refs, not from artwork.

graph_refs.description: MUST be non-empty — an item carries the graph, never a flat clip (moat rule).

highlight_id.description: The user's own capture behind this item; present only when source='user'. An auto-pick has no highlight and so no id — marking one would write resurfacing state against something that does not exist. Carried so an in-app renderer can advance the spaced ladder without parsing deep_link.

deep_link.description: Relative in-app link with jump-to-moment, e.g. /player/{slug}?t={sec}. For source='user' items it also carries &revisit={highlight_id} (url-encoded): arriving at the player with that marker records the review, which is how an EMAIL reader advances the spaced ladder at all. Without it the digest was write-only — it selected due items every week and nothing it sent could mark one reviewed, so the same five items were re-sent indefinitely.

source.description: 'user' = the user captured it; 'auto' = GI editor's-pick (FR3). Renderers MUST distinguish them.
